objective: Review commit 82f0f93 (the agent tool policy) for correctness and regressions before it ships.
scope: git diff 8f15386 82f0f93 -- packages/integrations/claude (diff of src and tests also at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/955f248d-75f2-5c36-9dd0-d4e898af84ee/scratchpad/review-src.diff); generated dist must equal a fresh build
constraints: Intent decision: every agent, root included, inherits all MCP tools via a disallowedTools denylist instead of a tools allowlist; native WebSearch and WebFetch are denied for all; each role keeps its previous built-ins; the root loses the Agent(holyagent:...) spawn allowlist on purpose; ToolSearch is kept for every agent so deferred MCP tools load. Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (tools omitted inherits every tool; disallowedTools applied first).
Read-only. Keep working until everything asked is done; stop and report when done. Make no version-control writes and no edits under .git/ or .holyagent/.
Report each finding with file:line, a concrete failing state, and blocking or non-blocking.

criteria.text: Each generated agent's effective built-in tools equal its previous ones apart from WebSearch and WebFetch (plus ToolSearch), and every MCP tool is inherited
No role gains a built-in that lets it break its role contract (a read-only role gaining Write, Edit, NotebookEdit or Bash; a specialist gaining Agent or Workflow; the root gaining Edit or Write)
Tests pin the policy, removed code leaves nothing dangling, and mise run verify passes on 82f0f93 (mise at /tmp/holyagent-validation/mise-bin)

result:
result: one blocking finding on the root; the 17 specialists meet the criteria, and `mise run verify` passes on 82f0f93.

findings:
1. **Blocking (criterion 1). The root inherits built-ins outside `BUILTIN_TOOLS`.** The root (`dist/agents/holyagent.md:disallowedTools`, built at `src/agents.ts:456`) is the main thread, so it is not a background subagent. Its effective built-ins therefore differ from its previous set.
   - **Failing state:** the denylist can only name the 27 tools in `BUILTIN_TOOLS` (`src/agents.ts:25`). It omits `EnterPlanMode`, `ExitPlanMode`, `ScheduleWakeup`, `CronCreate`, `CronDelete`, `CronList`, `RemoteTrigger`, `SendUserFile`, `PushNotification`, `SendFeedback`, `ShareOnboardingGuide`, `ReportFindings`, `EndConversation`, `WaitForMcpServers`, `ListAgents`, `ListMcpResourcesTool` and `ReadMcpResourceTool`.
   - **Source:** that list is the built-in table in https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference. I read it from the docs and did not run Claude Code, so which of these tools exist in a given session depends on version and plan.
   - **Test gap:** `tests/plugin.test.ts:450` filters on `BUILTIN_TOOLS`, so it cannot see any of them.
   - **Fix:** add these names to `BUILTIN_TOOLS` so the root denies them. The root root would keep only the tools it needs besides `ToolSearch`.
2. **Non-blocking, mitigated for specialists.** The omission above does not reach them. They set `background: true`, and the sub-agents docs (#available-tools) say a background subagent keeps only `Read, Grep, Glob, LSP, Bash, PowerShell, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, Skill, ToolSearch, EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree, Monitor, TaskStop, SendMessage, Artifact` (plus `SubagentHandback`) among built-ins. The first filter also removes `AskUserQuestion`, `EnterPlanMode`, `ExitPlanMode`, `ScheduleWakeup` and `Workflow`. All of the list that matters is in `BUILTIN_TOOLS`, so each specialist's effective built-ins match its previous set plus `ToolSearch`. That holds only while Claude Code keeps that filter.
3. **Non-blocking (the code-review's finding on `agents.ts:489`).** The root lost its `Agent(holyagent:...)` spawn allowlist and can now spawn `general-purpose`, which has `Write`/`Edit`. The Intent states this on purpose, and `docs/decisions.md` records it. No test pins "root keeps `Agent`" apart from the previous-set table, which does include it.
4. **Non-blocking (code-review, `agents.ts:428`).** Read-only roles now inherit write-capable MCP tools (github, Atlassian, Gmail). This follows from the Intent decision and the criteria cover built-ins only. Role text is the only guard. I did not run the roles against a live MCP session.
5. **Non-blocking (code-review, `agents.ts:87`).** The `MCP_LOADER` special case inside `denylist` is a minor style point.
6. **Optional (code-review, `agents.ts:17`).** `BUILTIN_TOOLS` and `NATIVE_WEB_TOOLS` are exported only for the test.
7. **Non-blocking (code-review, test weakness).** The previous-set table at `plugin.test.ts:408` is hard-coded from the old assertions, so it can fail and is not circular. The check `denied ⊆ BUILTIN_TOOLS` is tautological. Optional: assert that `BUILTIN_TOOLS` covers the documented built-in table, which would also have caught finding 1.
8. **Rejected (code-review):**
   - The `ROOT_BUILTINS` grant of `Bash` is unchanged from before, and "writes no files" was already the old claim.
   - `interface-inspection.md` still naming `mcp__t3-code__*` is fine, because those tools are now inherited, not listed.
   - Nothing is left dangling: grep finds no remaining uses of `inspectionTools`, `ROOT_T3_TOOLS`, `WEB` or `toolsOf`.

Criteria 2 and 3 pass. No read-only role gains `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` or `Bash`; `reviewer-code`, `reviewer-testing`, `worker-operations` and `worker-validation` keep `Bash` as before. No specialist gains `Agent` or `Workflow`, and the root denies `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit`, `PowerShell` and `WebSearch`/`WebFetch`. The only unfixed gap is the root's extra built-ins in finding 1.
